title: Jesu, Shepherd of the Sheep
description: Jesu, Shepherd of the Sheep in Tonic Solfa to RATISBON (WERNER), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 183.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7), and this page sets them to RATISBON (WERNER); any other Sevens, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-su, Shep-herd of the sheep, Pi-ty my un-set-tled soul! Guide, and nour-ish me, and keep, Till thy love shall make me whole: Give me per-fect sound-ness, give, Make me stead-fast-ly be-lieve.

lines: Guide, and nourish me, and keep,
Till thy love shall make me whole:
I am never at one stay,
Stablish with thy grace my heart.
Give me faith to hold me up,
Still my souls sure anchor be;
That I may be always thine,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to RATISBON (WERNER) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
